svg.title: Async-RBench: key evaluation mechanisms
svg.desc: Task-grounded paired evaluation. The same participant-safe task and benchmark-owned concurrent initial workstreams enter independent Linear and Async routes. A, B and C are illustrative independent subagents, not a fixed child-model pool or a required count. Private event rules cover eight benchmark event themes and define affected work and work to keep without revealing scoring truth to the model. Linear waits for every child to reach a terminal state before sending one stable result batch to the main agent. The Async example shows A and B still working while C produces a result; a document means result production rather than acceptance or correctness. The main agent keeps working and may adjust ongoing work, illustrated by its control arrow to A. C results undergo public submission checks and event send rules, may be staged, and then pass through sending, waiting and actual main-model presentation. The new result triggers update handling only when included in a launched model request; it does not cancel an in-flight request. Updating affected work and keeping valid work may happen together. Run records capture delivery, actual presentation, agent actions and event-boundary artifact digests. Hidden checks remain evaluator-private and do not suppress delivery. Linear BTS and Async BTS score their final states separately. DRS uses event and state evidence, half process and half event outcome, without claiming strict attribution to a single response window. Each metric aggregates repetitions and tasks before an equal-weight mean across event themes, with coverage reported separately.
